title: Pull requests from an agent

story: At 09:10 Nova, our ticket-to-PR agent, finishes RH-1234 and opens pull request #2512. Imagine it asked the frontend reviewers for a review at that moment. Dana, a teammate, opens the PR at 09:12 and sees CI still running. She opens it again at 09:35, and a unit test is red. At 09:52 everything is green, but by then she has looked three times at a PR that was not ready, and the next time Nova asks, she waits a day before she opens it.

People's attention is the scarcest thing in this whole loop. Every early ping spends some of the trust that makes people read agent PRs at all. There is a second problem hiding in the PR: its author is a bot, so GitHub cannot tell who asked for the work, and the person who asked must never be the one who approves it.
hook.question: When may an agent's PR ask people for their time, and what must it say about who asked for it?

p: A draft pull request is a normal PR with one difference: it is marked as not ready. GitHub requests no reviews for a draft and does not notify code owners, but CI still runs on every push. That makes a draft the right home for work in progress: the evidence keeps coming in, and nobody is disturbed.

So every agent PR is born a draft. Nova itself never holds a GitHub token. It asks the broker, the service that holds our GitHub credentials, to open the PR, and the broker takes the branch from the run's own record, never from the request, so a run cannot open a PR from someone else's branch. The title follows fcp's usual form: [FE] RH-1234: Empty projects table shows a No projects yet card.

notes.text: A short-lived token for this run's one repo. It is used here and never sent to the VM.
nova/RH-1234, from the run's scope. The request cannot choose another branch.
The body always ends with the Requested-by line; the last section is about it.
Always a draft: CI runs, nobody is pinged.
node_id is the PR's GraphQL ID, which marking it ready needs later.

read.h: Read the facts, not the claims
p: Nova may write "all tests pass" in its notes, but the decision to ping people must not rest on what the agent says. It rests on facts the gate reads for itself. The ready gate is a small step in the run that asks one question before anyone is pinged: is this PR clean?

The first facts are the required checks: the checks the main branch's rules demand before a merge. The gh CLI lists them with gh pr checks 2512 --required --json name,bucket. Every check has a bucket, a simple state: pass, fail, pending, skipping or cancel. Only pass and skipping are clean; pending blocks too, because a check that is still running may yet fail. One required check is special. The independent-approval check passes only after a person approves, and nobody approves a draft, so the gate leaves that one check out by name.

Then come the facts from the run itself: every QA check from the approved plan passed, and no important review finding is still open. If anything blocks, the PR stays a draft, the gate returns the list of reasons, and nobody hears a thing.

notes.text: The approval check cannot pass before review, and review starts only after ready. Leaving it out breaks that circle.
Only the required checks: those are the ones that decide whether a person could merge.
pending blocks as well as fail: a running check may still go red.
Any blocker: stay a draft, ping nobody, keep the reasons for the run's log.
Clean: ask the reviewer team for the area, for example the frontend guild for frontend/.

09:31  stays a draft: CI: [FRONTEND] - CI / unit-tests is fail

read.h: Leaving draft is one GraphQL call
p: GitHub's REST API can create a draft, but it cannot take a PR out of draft. That change exists only in GitHub's GraphQL API, as the mutation markPullRequestReadyForReview. A mutation is GraphQL's word for a call that changes something. It takes the PR's node ID, the global ID GraphQL uses for every object, which looks like PR_kwDO… and came back as node_id when the PR was created. The command gh pr ready 2512 sends this same mutation.

The broker checks first that PR #2512 belongs to this run, because a run may mark only its own PR ready. Right after that, people hear about it once: the reviewer team is asked for a review, the requester gets a Slack message, and the Jira ticket is assigned back to the requester, so a person owns it again. The agent never approves and never merges; its GitHub App has no permission for either.

notes.text: One variable: the PR's node ID, such as PR_kwDODKw3uc8AAAABIUZlvw.
Ask for isDraft back to confirm the change: false means ready.

read.h: The last line names who asked
p: GitHub already stops the author of a PR from approving it. On an agent PR, though, the author is rhino-ai-agents[bot], our GitHub App, so that rule protects nothing: you (Sean) asked for RH-1234, and GitHub has no idea. That is why the last line of every agent PR body is Requested-by: @sean, written by the platform from your entry in the people file, never by the model.

A required check, independent-approval, reads that line and refuses an approval from the person it names. If the line is missing, the check fails instead of passing, which is called failing closed: when the input a check needs is not there, it says no. The lesson on checks an agent cannot weaken looks at that check more closely; here it is enough that the PR always carries the line, so the gate in the lab treats a missing line as a blocker too.

notes.text: The same pattern the approval check uses to read the line.
The requester is known by Jira accountId; GitHub needs the login, so the people file maps one to the other.
No mapping, no PR: a guessed requester is worse than an error.

lab.title: Read a PR like the ready gate
lab.goal: Read a real draft PR's checks with gh, then run a small ready gate over three moments in the life of PR #2512 and make it insist on the Requested-by line.

guess.q: At 09:15 PR #2512's required checks are: lint pass, unit-tests pending, build pending, locked-checks pass, independent-approval fail. Should the gate mark it ready?

options.text: Yes: nothing has failed except the approval check, which is normal before review.
options.why: The approval check is indeed left out, but pending is not clean. A running check may still go red, and people would be pinged for nothing.

options.text: No: unit-tests and build are still pending, so it stays a draft and nobody is pinged.
options.why: Only pass and skipping are clean. The gate waits for the facts before it spends anyone's attention.

options.text: No: independent-approval failed, so the PR is broken.
options.why: That check cannot pass before a person approves, and nobody approves a draft. The gate skips it on purpose.

Make the gate insist on the Requested-by line. Save the PR body below as pr-body.md (it has no Requested-by line yet). Give readyGate a third input, the body, and push the blocker "no Requested-by line: the approval check would fail closed" when the line is missing; read the pattern from the lesson. ### What changes

### References
- RH-1234

lab.fix: CI was slow last week, so someone added c.bucket !== "pending" to the filter "to get PRs to reviewers sooner". Make that change and run the gate on checks-0915.json: it now says ready. In real life, the reviewer team was pinged at 09:15, and at 09:31 the unit test went red on the PR they were reading. Remove the change and say in one sentence why pending must block.
explain: Why does an agent PR start as a draft instead of asking for review at once?
Why does the gate leave the independent-approval check out, and why only that one?
The PR's author is a bot. Why does that make the Requested-by line necessary?
lab.done: The gate keeps #2512 a draft at 09:15 and 09:31, marks it ready at 09:52 only with the Requested-by line, and every gh command you ran only read.

check.q: A required check's bucket is pending. What does the ready gate do?

options.text: Keeps the PR a draft, pings nobody, and lists the pending check as a blocker
options.why: Only pass and skipping are clean. A check that is still running may still fail.

options.text: Marks it ready, because nothing has failed yet
options.why: Then people may be pinged for a PR that turns red ten minutes later, which is exactly the trust the gate protects.

options.text: Re-runs the check until it passes
options.why: The gate only reads checks. Re-running CI is never the agent's job.

check.q: How does the broker take an agent's PR out of draft?

options.text: With the REST call that updates a PR, setting draft to false
options.why: The REST API cannot leave draft. That change exists only in GraphQL.
Labels do not change the draft state.

options.text: With the GraphQL mutation markPullRequestReadyForReview and the PR's node ID
options.why: gh pr ready sends the same mutation. The node ID came back when the PR was created.

check.q: You asked for RH-1234, and Nova's GitHub App opened the PR. Why is GitHub's own rule ("authors cannot approve their own PR") not enough?

options.text: Because GitHub's rule does not apply to drafts
options.why: Drafts cannot be approved at all, but the problem appears once the PR is ready.

options.text: Because the author is the bot, so GitHub does not know you asked, and you could approve alone; the Requested-by line tells the approval check
options.why: The independent-approval check reads the line and refuses your approval, so a second person always looks.

options.text: Because bots cannot be authors on GitHub
options.why: GitHub Apps can open PRs; that is exactly why the author is the bot and not the person.

p: Agent PRs are opened through the broker's small allow-list of GitHub actions: create a draft, mark the run's own PR ready, view, diff, read checks and comment on its own PR. It never merges, approves or changes settings. The body is rendered from the run's evidence pack with the pr-story headings, keeps ### References with the Jira link, and always ends with Requested-by: @<login> from config/people.yaml; for a routine, the line names the routine's owner.

The ready gate is an orchestrator activity. When it finds the PR clean it runs gh pr ready through the broker, requests the reviewer team by area (frontend-guild for frontend/**, backend-guild for cloud/** and client/**), sets the Nova state to PR open, posts in the Slack thread and assigns the Jira ticket back to the requester. If main fails the same check, Nova links main's failing run in the PR instead of looping.

tickets.why: The ready gate: required checks, QA results, judges and findings, then gh pr ready and the reviewer team.
The PR body from the evidence pack, the pr-story headings, ### References, and the Requested-by line.
The broker's GitHub allow-list: drafts, its own PR ready, read checks, comment; never merge or approve.
The independent-approval check that reads the Requested-by line and fails closed without it.

words.plain: A PR marked as not ready: CI runs, but no reviews are requested and nobody is notified.
A check the branch's rules demand before a merge. The ready gate reads only these.
The simple state gh gives each check: pass, fail, pending, skipping or cancel.
The step that marks a PR ready only when checks, QA results and findings are all clean.
A GitHub object's global GraphQL ID, like PR_kwDO…; GraphQL mutations need it.
The last line of an agent PR body, naming the person who asked; that person can never approve it.

review.q: List what the ready gate reads before it marks a PR ready.
review.a: The required checks (pass or skipping only, independent-approval left out), the QA results from the approved plan, and the important review findings (all handled). Plus the Requested-by line must be there.

review.q: A teammate wants Nova to request reviewers when it opens the PR, "to save time". What do you answer?
review.a: Reviewers would see PRs with running or red CI and stop trusting Nova's pings. The draft costs nobody anything; the gate pings once, when the facts say it is clean.

review.q: Who is on the Requested-by line of a CI fixer's PR, and why?
review.a: The routine's owner, because they are the person answerable for the work, so they must not be the one approval.

remember: An agent's PR stays a draft until the gate reads clean facts, and its last line always names the person who asked.
